first_prompt: Work on the brief in `llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md`. Read it in full now, even if you have read it before: it is the instruction for this cycle and every cycle of this loop, and what you remember of it

commits.summary: tool_time.py: where loops' time went, by category, loop and cargo test binary, from the redacted logs
commits.body:
Phase 1 step 1 of the test-cost brief (llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md). llm-dlc/tools/tool_time.py turns the 2026-11-15 ad-hoc time analysis, whose scripts were not kept, into a tool Phase 5 runs again on the next loop. It finds loop sessions from the briefs' Loop settings and the loop summaries (a stream counts towards its loop), reads each session's redacted log (with --fetch, the published copy of one not stored here, checked against its sha256), and reports: active and model time (metrics.py's), blocked time per batch of parallel calls (counted once, given to the call that finished last, calls over two hours left out) by category, waits on commands started in the background, per-loop shares, cargo's compile and per-binary test timings, and full-suite, debug and release spreads. Markdown or --format json.

Verified: test_tool_time.py (10 tests on made-up logs: classification, batching, the two-hour cut, background waits by task id and by redirected file, cargo output parsing, full-suite detection, discovery, an end-to-end JSON report, and fetch refusing content that doesn't match its name) and test_metrics.py pass. Run on the measurement's 26 sessions it reproduces the compile/test split exactly (936 timed runs, 0.9h compiling, 8.2h tests) and the slow files' order (conformance.rs, observations.rs, integration.rs, alignment.rs, application_core.rs).

The brief is out of date in places: its 'Where it starts from' totals came from those scripts, under other definitions. This tool gives active 116h, tools 47.8h, cargo test 20.8h, proofs inline 4.7h; and for full-suite debug runs 91 calls, 14% of cargo test time, median 11s, p90 579s, against the brief's 542 runs, 48%, median 17s and p90 136s (all debug runs: 788, 44%, median 8s, p90 82s). It finds 26 loop sessions, not 27. Done-when's 60-second budget is unaffected; Phase 5 should compare against this tool's numbers. Progress records the command line.

commits.summary: test-cost brief revised: no measuring run, tiers from past runs and estimates; the loop cut to tags, lint and guidance
commits.body: The user stopped the test-cost loop in its second cycle, as it was about to queue a measuring job that past results put at about 3 hours, and asked that nothing be re-run to measure, so that the stream conductor can follow soon. The brief now takes each test's tier from past sessions' timings, past pipeline results and what the test spawns, marking estimates as such; keeps the measuring tool as one to write but not run; and adds no #[ignore] to any test that runs by default today, listing those for the next loop as 'retier: pending'. The proxies, the retiering of the five slow files, the reuse of passed results and the JBMC cache move to a later test-cost loop (new decision 9). Phases are now: tools and inventory, tags and lint, guidance. The loop's uncommitted step-2 files (test_costs.py, install-nextest.sh, nextest.toml) were kept out of this commit and left in the working copy for the loop to finish.

commits.summary: test_costs.py: the per-test cost measuring tool, written and tested but not run; cargo-nextest installed, hash-pinned
commits.body: Phase 1 step 2 of the test-cost brief, as revised after the user stopped the run before its measuring job. lib/tools/test_costs.py measures what each test costs: a warm plain cargo test for the default run's wall time, then every Rust test under cargo-nextest, one process each (debug for default tests, release for ignored ones), and every Python test file test by test. For each test it records time, CPU, peak memory and the processes spawned (sampled from /proc), and writes lib/tests/costs.json with the tier each test measures into (unit: no subprocess, under 1 s; tool: under 10 s and 1 GB; proof: JBMC/TLC or over those). lib/.config/nextest.toml defines only a measure profile that runs each test under the tool's watch wrapper; plain cargo test and nextest's default profile are unaffected. lib/tools/install-nextest.sh installs cargo-nextest 0.9.151 from its github.com release, pinned to the sha256 that both the release's .sha256 asset and GitHub's asset digest give.

commits.body: The test of test_costs.tool_name used /home/u/.local/bin/tlc as a made-up TLC launcher path, which the redaction scan flags as another user's home directory (finding bca79831, other-home-dir, in this session's log). The test now uses /opt/tools/bin/tlc, and the finding is proposed for the allow list as a false positive, for the user to approve. Verified: python3 lib/tools/test_test_costs.py passes (12 tests).

commits.summary: test_costs.py estimate: the cost inventory of every Rust and Python test, from past runs and what each test calls, running nothing
commits.body:
lib/tests/costs.json is now generated by `python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py estimate` (about 20 s, no test run). It lists the 642 Rust tests and 782 Python tests, one per line, each with a tier, what it calls, its cost and that cost's sources, and why. A new module, lib/tools/cost_inventory.py, does the reading:
- The Rust tests come from lib/src and lib/tests with strings and comments blanked. The list matched `cargo test -- --list` exactly, a check run once that only lists. The Python tests come from ast.
- What a test calls is read from its body and the same-file helpers it reaches: JBMC through Engine::Jbmc or Auto, equivalence::run or property::run without the native engine, has_jbmc() or missing("JBMC"); TLC through run_tlc or tlc_command; javac, java, the binary, a stand-in script, or Command::new.
- What a test cost comes from the cargo output kept in 22 redacted session logs, through tool_time.py, and from 52 past jobs' logs in verification/results. A section that ran one test gives that test's time, one that ran several bounds each of them, and "running for over 60 seconds" bounds a test from below. Python's comes from runs of a single file or test.

A test's tier is the higher of what it calls and what it took alone. A tier no past run settles is marked estimated, with the reason. A proof-tier test that runs by default is marked retier: pending.
- Rust: 268 unit, 299 tool and 75 proof. The proof tests are the 12 ignored ones and 63 retier pending, 45 of those in integration.rs. 226 Rust tiers are estimates.
- Python: 611 unit, 171 tool, no proof, and 394 estimates.

The brief asked for lib/tests/costs.json "and the same for Python": both are in that one file, as the rust and python lists.

Known gap, left to the next loop: measure's inventory still keys rows by nextest's binary id, so it must be made to write the same shape before it replaces these estimates.

commits.summary: Rust test tiers: the tool_tier! helper, test_costs.py tag, and the twelve ignore reasons as cost:proof tags
commits.body: Phase 2 step 4 of llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md, first part. lib/src/test_tier.rs adds tool_tier!(), the first statement of a tool-tier test, and tool_tier!(pending) for a proof-tier test that still runs by default (retier: pending in lib/tests/costs.json). Both return at once under JVMCONTRACT_TEST_TIER=unit and do nothing without it; any other value than unit, tool or proof panics. A new subcommand, python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py tag FILE ..., gives each test the call its inventory row asks for, and takes it off unit-tier and ignored tests. A second run changes nothing. heap.rs (48 tool-tier tests), conformance.rs (6 tool, 3 pending) and preparation.rs (none) are tagged. Their twelve #[ignore] reasons now read 'cost:proof: WHAT IT RUNS, ~TIME; proxy: TEST', with times from past jobs. The heap proxies are the native-engine tests that run the same cases. The conformance proxy is the own-checker corpus run, itself retier: pending. The benchmark says 'proxy: none yet'. The inventory was regenerated (644 Rust tests, with test_tier's two). A second regeneration was byte-identical.

commits.summary: Rust test tiers: every tool-tier and retier-pending test calls tool_tier!, 305 more across 27 files
commits.body:
python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py tag, run over the 22 remaining files in lib/tests/ and the five in lib/src/ with tool-tier or retier-pending tests, added 245 tool_tier!() calls and 60 tool_tier!(pending) calls (crate::tool_tier!() in lib/src/). With the previous commit's 57, all 299 tool-tier tests and 63 retier-pending tests in lib/tests/costs.json now call the helper first. A second tag over all 30 files changes nothing. Under JVMCONTRACT_TEST_TIER=unit those tests return at once. Without the variable nothing changes, and no test runs less by default.

The regenerated inventory's Rust rows are unchanged. It now also lists the two Tagging tests in lib/tools/test_cost_inventory.py, which the previous commit's inventory had left out because they were written after its last estimate.

Verified: cargo build --tests is clean, apart from foundations.rs's three unused imports, which were there before. JVMCONTRACT_TEST_TIER=unit cargo test --no-fail-fast passes in 27 s. The default cargo test --no-fail-fast passes: 632 passed, 12 ignored, 0 failed, in 11 min 4 s. Progress lists for review the unit-tier tests that are still slow under the unit-only run (the library's and summaries.rs's), and two lib/src/jbmc.rs tests that are tool tier only because their text holds a shebang.

commits.summary: Python test tiers: the @cost decorator, test_costs.py tag for Python, and the 54 tool-tier tests tagged
commits.body:
lib/tools/cost_tier.py adds @cost("tool" | "pending" | "proof"), Python's counterpart of tool_tier!. Under TEST_COST=unit the tool and pending tests are skipped with a reason; proof is skipped unless TEST_COST=proof; unset, nothing that runs today is skipped; a misspelt value raises. The inventory's Python reading counted any mention of subprocess as a spawn. It now counts a call, so 117 tests that only patch subprocess away, refuse Popen or build a CompletedProcess for a mock moved from tool to unit (test_build.py 81, test_workflow.py 26, and others). Python is now 790 tests, 736 unit and 54 tool; Rust rows are unchanged. test_costs.py tag now decorates Python test methods as their rows ask and manages the import of cost. It tagged 54 tests in 12 files, and a second run over all 31 Python test files changes nothing. lib/README.md's Tests section describes the decorator.

Verified: test_cost_inventory.py (19 tests, unit tier) covers the decorator, the narrower check, tagging, a U+2028 in a file (str.splitlines splits there, ast doesn't) and a decorator inside a string. The 12 tagged files and test_cost_inventory.py, each run by default and under TEST_COST=unit, all pass. The default runs skip nothing, and the unit runs skip exactly the 54 tagged tests. Rust is untouched, so cargo test wasn't rerun. test_runtime.py, test_pipeline.py and test_performance.py stay slow under TEST_COST=unit, because their tests spawn through the module under test, which the static reading can't see. This is listed for review in Progress.

The brief is out of date in one place: 'Where it starts from' counts 28 Python test_*.py files; the inventory now finds 31.

commits.summary: Test tiers: one way to run each, test_costs.py run --tier default|unit|proof, documented in lib/README.md
commits.body:
Phase 2 step 6 of llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md. python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run runs cargo test in lib/ and then each Python test file lib/tests/costs.json lists, in its own process, with one line per file and the full output on failure. --tier default (what runs inline) sets JVMCONTRACT_TEST_TIER and TEST_COST to tool, which is the same as unset, so nothing is skipped that ran before. --tier unit sets them to unit. --tier proof runs cargo test --release -- --ignored and only the Python tests tagged @cost("proof"), of which there are none yet. --only, --test and --dry-run narrow a run.

lib/README.md's Tests section opens with the tiers and the two inline commands. It writes down the proof tier's pipeline.py submit command: 4 CPUs, 8G, 1.5 h, from past jobs' times. That command was checked with --dry-run only, and no job was written. The measure paragraph's heap and conformance times are corrected to the inventory's.

Verified: test_test_costs.py (16 tests, 4 of them new for run) passes by default and under TEST_COST=unit. run --only python passed 30 of 31 files by default, skipping nothing, and 30 of 31 under --tier unit. The Rust code is unchanged, so cargo test wasn't run. The inventory was regenerated.

Found, and recorded for review in the brief's Progress: examples/tools/test_economics.py fails by default, apart from this loop, because examples 287 and 289 to 291 have no subject.file. The inventory misses 27 of test_runtime_upstream.py's 30 tests, whose classes inherit a TestCase from test_runtime; step 7 starts by listing them. Three heap proof tests failed their last jobs (VF-018 reruns).

commits.summary: Test tiers: the lint, test_costs.py lint, in the default run as tests/tiers.rs and tools/test_tier_lint.py
commits.body:
Phase 2 step 7 of llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md. The lint checks four things against the sources and lib/tests/costs.json: every ignore reason is a cost:proof tag with a proxy that runs by default, or proxy: none yet for a test on the inventory's list; no test outside the proof tier calls JBMC or TLC, except the retier: pending tests; the inventory and the sources name the same tests, and what it records of each is current; and every tool_tier! or @cost tag is the one its row asks for. It runs in the default run twice, both at the unit tier. lib/tests/tiers.rs is in cargo test and checks what it can read without following a test into its helpers. lib/tools/test_tier_lint.py is in the Python run and checks all of it for both languages, with ten more tests of the lint on made-up sources. lib/README.md's Tests section says what each problem asks for.

Joining the retier: pending or proxy: none yet list is now for a person: estimate keeps the tests already listed. A new JBMC or TLC test that runs by default, or a new proxy: none yet, gets an unlisted row, which the lint refuses until a person runs estimate --list FILE::NAME. A Python proof tag now carries its reason, @cost("proof", "...; proxy: Class.test"), and the lint refuses an unconditional @unittest.skip. The Python listing now follows a TestCase base imported from another file of the repository. That lists the 27 tests of examples/tools/targets/test_runtime_upstream.py the inventory had missed, 15 of them now @cost("tool"). The Rust listing went from 13 s to 0.9 s, with the same result for every test.

Verified: tiers.rs, test_tier_lint.py, test_cost_inventory.py and test_test_costs.py pass by default and under the unit tier. test_runtime_upstream.py passes under unit, with 15 tests skipped. The default run (test_costs.py run) was run once: cargo test 634 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored; Python 32 of 33 files passed. The failing file is examples/tools/test_economics.py, which was already failing before this loop (KeyError 'file' in build.app_of on examples 287 and 289-291; recorded in Progress last cycle). No job is needed: nothing that runs by default was skipped or ignored.

commits.summary: Test tiers: the guidance, in CLAUDE.md, the brief template, verification/README.md and lib/README.md
commits.body:
Phase 3 step 8 of llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md. CLAUDE.md gets a Tests section: the unit, tool and proof tiers; the default run (python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run) is what runs inline; the proof tier runs as a job for the tests a change touched, with decision 4's one exception stated narrowly; write the cheapest test that shows the behaviour, and give a new proof-tier test a tag, a reason and a proxy; adding a test to the retier: pending or proxy: none yet lists is for a person. The brief template's standing rule names the tiers instead of conformance cases on a real java. verification/README.md says the slow tests are the proof tier plus the 63 retier: pending tests until they move, and its estimate table gives the proof tier's job. lib/README.md's Tests section gains Writing a test.

The brief is slightly out of date: decision 4 lets an agent run a proof test inline when the inventory measures it under a minute, but the inventory measures nothing yet. The guidance reads it as a row recording a past run of that test alone under a minute (kind: run alone, not estimated). Only Markdown changed, and no test reads these files, so no test was run.

commits.summary: Test cost: the for-review list in Progress, and Status done
commits.body:
Phase 3 step 9 of llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md. The brief's Progress now lists what a person and the next test-cost loop should review, counted from lib/tests/costs.json without running any test. It covers the tiers with no past timing at all (Rust 2, Python 162, by file) and those that past runs bound only from above (Rust 228, Python 274). It gives the retier: pending list by file (63 Rust tests, ten of them proof tier only because a past run was slow) and the proxy: none yet list (the preparation benchmark). It ends with the findings from the tagging: conformance's proxy is itself retier: pending, three heap jobs may not have run JBMC though those tests qualify for the inline exception, three heap tests fail their jobs at about an hour, two jbmc.rs tests are tool tier only because of a shebang, there are slow unit binaries, the Python reading misses spawns inside the module under test, measure's inventory writes another row shape, and test_economics.py was already failing. Every criterion of Done when holds, so Status is done. Only the brief's Markdown changed, and no test reads it, so no test was run.

The brief is out of date in places, left as written outside Progress: decision 4 says the inline exception applies when 'the inventory measures it under a minute', but the inventory measures nothing yet, so the guidance reads that as a past run of the test alone (kind 'run alone'). Decision 6 gives the slow files' proxies to 'Phase 4', a phase of the first draft that decision 9 deferred to the next loop. The Direction's lint 'in the default run' is in place, but 'Where it starts from' still counts 384 integration tests and 258 unit tests, against 646 Rust tests now.

commits.summary: Fixes after the test-cost loop: app_of for real-world examples without a file, Fable 5.2 pricing, the brief's stale passages
commits.body:
examples/tools/build.py's app_of read example['subject']['file'], which the schema requires only of constructed examples. The real-world Spring Security examples 287 and 289-291 name only a system and symbol, so economics.recorded() raised KeyError 'file' and examples/tools/test_economics.py failed by default (4 errors), as it had since before the test-cost loop. app_of now returns None when the example names no file, as its docstring already said for an example on no known app; every caller handles None.

llm-dlc/pricing.json gains claude-fable-5-2 at the API list price, $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, $0.20 cache reads, and cache writes at the file's 1.25x and 2x input ($10 and $16), so session 0c1ceb11's 31 Fable 5.2 calls stop counting as $0. claude-sonnet-5-5's cache read is corrected from $0.20 to its list price of $0.10. as_of moves to 2026-11-15. Every metrics.json is recomputed on the next sync.

llm-dlc/loops/test-cost.md, outside Progress: 'Where it starts from' now says its counts were the loop's start and gives the end's (646 Rust, 833 Python in 31 files); decision 4's inline exception reads as the guidance does, a past run of the test alone under a minute; decision 6's proxies go to the next test-cost loop instead of a Phase 4 that no longer exists.

Verified: test_economics.py passes (11 tests), and so do test_alignment.py and test_metrics.py, the other callers and readers. The default Python run (test_costs.py run --only python) passed 32 of 32 files, and test_costs.py lint agrees. No Rust changed, so cargo test was not rerun.
